metrics.description: Fraction of hidden key-dependent leaky signals (key_mix_reg, sbox_out_reg) correctly flagged as leaking in the submitted report, versus false positives on non-leaky signals.
metrics.name: leakage_detection_accuracy

metrics.description: Fraction of all signals named in design_brief.md that appear with well-formed entries (signal_name, hd_variance, flagged) in the submission, ensuring the analysis is complete rather than partial.
metrics.name: fault_coverage

metrics.description: Fraction of recommendations that target genuinely leaky signals with a recognized countermeasure technique, penalizing recommendations aimed at non-leaky signals or vague/no-mechanism advice.
metrics.name: hardening_precision

hidden_spec.ground_truth: The datapath has a key_mix_reg (post XOR of plaintext and round key) and an sbox_out_reg (registered output of the S-box lookup applied to key_mix_reg). Both show power-model Hamming-distance variance that correlates strongly with key bits across varying plaintext, because the transition depends on the previous and current values of a key-dependent intermediate. The plaintext_reg alone (before key mixing) and the final round_out_reg (after a linear diffusion layer that is called out in the brief as already balanced) do not leak key-dependent information under the given power model to the same degree. Correct hardening isolates or masks key_mix_reg and sbox_out_reg (e.g., boolean masking of the S-box, or dual-rail/precharge on those two registers specifically), not the whole datapath uniformly.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: evaluate.py computes hd_variance for key_mix_reg and plaintext_reg by re-simulating round_datapath.v across the vector set in testbench_hd_trace.v with several fixed round-key values and confirms key_mix_reg's variance is materially higher (data+key dependent) than plaintext_reg's (data-only). It checks the submitted flagged/hd_variance for key_mix_reg matches this expectation within tolerance.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly flag key_mix_reg as leaking (flagged=true) with a hd_variance value that is substantially higher (report must state or imply it is an outlier) relative to plaintext_reg's hd_variance.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Same re-simulation approach applied to sbox_out_reg; evaluator checks flagged=true and hd_variance is within tolerance of the recomputed ground-truth value, and that flagged=false is treated as a miss.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly flag sbox_out_reg as leaking, since its transitions are a nonlinear key-dependent function of key_mix_reg.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: evaluator checks that recommendations targeting round_out_reg/plaintext_reg are not present as the sole or top-ranked recommendation, and that key_mix_reg and sbox_out_reg appear among the top-ranked (by hd_variance) flagged entries.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must NOT flag round_out_reg or plaintext_reg as the primary leakage points, or if flagged, must not recommend masking them instead of key_mix_reg/sbox_out_reg (avoiding a report that dilutes hardening effort onto non-leaky signals).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: evaluator performs a keyword/technique match on the 'technique' field for entries targeting key_mix_reg/sbox_out_reg against an allowed-technique list (masking, dual-rail, precharge, isolation, hiding, blinding); rejects vague or missing techniques.
security_requirements.requirement: Hardening recommendations for key_mix_reg and sbox_out_reg must propose a recognized countermeasure (e.g. boolean/arithmetic masking of the S-box input/output, dual-rail logic, random precharge, or hiding via balanced routing) rather than generic advice like 'add more logic' with no isolation/masking mechanism named.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker with access to power/EM traces of the running datapath performs differential/correlation power analysis (DPA/CPA) using a Hamming-distance leakage model on register transitions, hypothesizing key values and correlating predicted HD against measured trace variance to recover round key bits without knowing the key.

constraints: All RTL must be synthesizable Verilog-2001, single clock, synchronous active-high reset, no vendor primitives.
The testbench and power model must be fully self-contained and runnable with iverilog/vvp without external libraries.
Do not modify any file under inputs/; all analysis results go only into submission/vulnerability_report.json.
The S-box must be implemented as a combinational lookup table (case statement or array) so its output is a pure function of its input each cycle.
expected_outputs: submission/vulnerability_report.json listing each analyzed register/net with its measured Hamming-distance variance across input vectors
A ranked list of the top signals with highest variance/correlation to plaintext or key bits
Concrete hardening recommendations (masking, isolation, dual-rail, etc.) tied to each flagged signal

functional_requirements.requirement: The report JSON must include an entry for every register named in round_datapath.v's port/signal list (as documented in design_brief.md), each with fields: signal_name (string), hd_variance (number), flagged (boolean).

For at least one input vector set specified in testbench_hd_trace.v, the reported hd_variance values must be internally consistent: signals driven directly by combinational functions of the plaintext alone (e.g. registered plaintext bits before any key mixing) must have hd_variance reported within +/-5% of the value computed by re-running the provided testbench and power_model.md formula on that signal.

The submission file must be valid JSON conforming exactly to the schema in response_format, with top-level keys 'signals' (array) and 'recommendations' (array); no other top-level keys are required but extras are ignored.
Each recommendation entry must reference at least one signal_name that also appears in the 'signals' array (no dangling references).

public_spec.interface: Submission file: submission/vulnerability_report.json. Required JSON schema: {"signals": [{"signal_name": string, "hd_variance": number, "flagged": boolean, "notes": string (optional)}], "recommendations": [{"target_signal": string, "technique": string, "rationale": string}]}. 'signal_name' values must exactly match identifiers declared in round_datapath.v (module ports and internal reg/wire declarations documented in design_brief.md). evaluate.py reads inputs/round_datapath.v, inputs/sbox_table.v, inputs/testbench_hd_trace.v, inputs/power_model.md to (a) check field presence/format (FR grading) and (b) optionally re-simulate via iverilog/vvp to cross-check reported hd_variance numbers and flagged status against hidden ground-truth leaky signals (SR grading).
public_spec.objective: Analyze the provided RTL crypto round datapath (a small substitution-permutation round with a key-mixing stage and an S-box lookup) together with the accompanying switching-activity (Hamming-distance) trace model, and produce a structured report identifying which registers/nets show measurable data-dependent switching activity across the simulated input set, plus recommended design changes to reduce that dependency.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON file at submission/vulnerability_report.json matching the schema given in 'interface'. All numeric fields are plain JSON numbers (not strings); booleans are JSON true/false.

title: Power side-channel leakage localization in an S-box datapath
